title: Kotlin for JavaScript
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of kotlin for javascript using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates kotlin for javascript.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Kotlin for JavaScript** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks. Use the subtopics—Kotlin/JS Project Setup, JavaScript Interoperability, Packaging and Integrating JavaScript Output—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with kotlin/js project setup. Then compare it with javascript interoperability. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Kotlin/JS Project Setup
items.text: Kotlin/JS Project Setup is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: JavaScript Interoperability
items.text: JavaScript Interoperability means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Packaging and Integrating JavaScript Output
items.text: Packaging and Integrating JavaScript Output is one part of kotlin for javascript. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Kotlin for JavaScript removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates kotlin for javascript. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving kotlin/js project setup.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain kotlin for javascript without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Kotlin/JS Project Setup. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
